answer: Behavioral lineage tracing. Each agent action records a lightweight parent pointer to the prior action that triggered it, forming a provenance thread. After the fact, auditors cluster these threads into a trellis of correlated behavior and flag accounts whose action histories share too many upstream ancestors—a signature of farmed identities. Flagged clusters lose standing and are quarantined, so an attacker must fabricate distinct, independently grounded histories for every puppet, buying genuine activity and delay per identity. A single shared origin cannot harbor many accounts undetected.
